summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD, CABG, COPD, CVA, and hypothyroidism was admitted for left leg swelling and chest pain. Workup revealed no pulmonary embolism or acute cardiac ischemia. Abdominal pain was attributed to urinary retention with a markedly distended bladder, which improved after Foley catheter placement. He developed transient atrial fibrillation with RVR, managed with rate control, but medication was stopped due to bradycardia. A new cough and chest X-ray changes led to treatment for mild bacterial pneumonia. He failed two voiding trials, so was discharged home with a catheter and tamsulosin. Chronic issues like diverticulosis, SMA stenosis, and an incidental L4 vertebral finding were noted for outpatient follow-up. He stabilized, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged in stable condition with home health services.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
